findings.quoted_text: (R1) exhibit a datum D in the declared generic set G with not-P(D) - this refutes outright, because the statement is universal over G
findings.why: G is existentially quantified and never fixed; the schema's own genericity.membership_ruling says it does not decide membership of an individual datum, and G = X is comeager, so 'D in G' constrains nothing. A single datum with not-P(D) is exactly tier_2's witness, which tier_2.labelling_required marks as refuting only the strengthening. Route R1 contradicts visibility.observability_note and proof_obligations repeats it. Only non-meagerness of the not-P set (route R2) refutes the class.
findings.minimal_repair: Delete R1 or replace it with 'the datum lies in every comeager set (equivalently the not-P set is non-meager)'; keep R2 as the only class-refuting route and drop 'D in G' from proof_obligations.

findings.quoted_text: every future-inextendible causal geodesic of finite affine length lies outside the causal past of every point of I+, i.e. inside the black-hole region B = M minus J^-(I+)
findings.why: The 'i.e.' asserts not-visible iff gamma contained in B, but the formal predicate is not-visible iff for every q in I+, gamma is not contained in J^-(q) intersect M. B-containment is strictly stronger: a timelike geodesic that starts in the exterior (early points in J^-(I+)), crosses the horizon and ends at the singularity in finite proper time is not visible (no single q sees its terminal part) yet is not contained in B. Together with non_vacuity.condition this false equivalence entails B non-empty for a member of G, i.e. black-hole-region non-emptiness, which conclusion.forbidden_strengthenings[0] forbids.
findings.minimal_repair: Restate the negation as 'for every q in I+, gamma is not contained in J^-(q) intersect M' and delete the 'i.e. inside B'; if B-containment is intended, declare it a strictly stronger additional hypothesis.

findings.quoted_text: a measure-zero set can be comeager (e.g. the irrationals in R are comeager and have full measure; a comeager null set exists by intersecting open dense sets of shrinking measure)
findings.why: For pair [full_measure, residual_comeager] the required witness is a full-measure set that is NOT comeager (a meager full-measure set). The irrationals are comeager AND full-measure, so the example witnesses no non-transfer; its first clause restates the opposite direction. The correct witness is recorded externally (flash-15 c0_transfer_failures_block.yaml W2).
findings.minimal_repair: Replace the witness with: let G be a comeager Lebesgue-null set (intersection of open dense U_n with mu(U_n) < 1/n); then X minus G is meager and has full measure.

findings.quoted_text: norm topology of the weighted Sobolev product H^s_delta x H^{s-1}_{delta+1} ; X^{s,delta}_vac(AF): ... modulo asymptotically-identity diffeomorphisms ; G = intersection over n >= 1 of U_n, each U_n open and dense in the named topology
findings.why: Comeagerness is not well-defined. (a) G is contained in X_vac(AF) but the named topology is the product topology; under the literal product reading X_vac(AF) is a closed subset with empty interior (the constraints are non-trivial), hence nowhere dense and meager, so no G contained in X_vac is comeager and the class statement is false for every (s,delta); the intended subspace topology is not stated. (b) The named norm topology is not a topology on the declared ambient space (data modulo diffeomorphisms), whose construction the schema itself calls an open gap; 'open and dense in the named topology' is ambiguous between X_vac and the product. (c) Non-emptiness and Baire-ness of the ambient space are never asserted, so a comeager G may be empty in a way the schema does not detect.
findings.minimal_repair: Fix the ambient space (constraint subspace, or its quotient with the quotient topology), state that open/dense/comeager are relative to that space, and require the space to be non-empty and Baire (or make non-emptiness an explicit hypothesis).

findings.quoted_text: a countable union of finite-codimension submanifolds can be dense with empty interior; codimension control is neither necessary nor sufficient for comeagerness
findings.why: finite_codimension_complement is defined nowhere in this schema (rule_spec lists the token without semantics). Under the natural reading (failure set contained in a finite/countable union of finite-codimension submanifolds) each such submanifold is nowhere dense, so the failure set is meager and the good set IS comeager: the control is sufficient, making 'neither necessary nor sufficient' false. The row's direction (comeager does not imply fcc) is defensible; the witness is not; external adjudication records [finite_codimension_complement, residual_comeager] as transfer_holds.
findings.minimal_repair: Define the notion in the schema, keep the direction 'comeager does not imply fcc' with a comeager-set-of-infinite-codimension witness, and delete the false sufficiency claim.

findings.quoted_text: comeager and measure-zero are compatible: the complement of a fat Cantor set is open dense with arbitrarily small measure; a comeager set can be Lebesgue-null
findings.why: A fat Cantor set is closed and nowhere dense, so it cannot have full measure; its complement has positive measure, hence is not null. The example shows 'arbitrarily small positive measure', not compatibility with measure zero; it is flash-15's witness for the different pair [open_dense_escape, full_measure]. The claim itself is true via the countable-intersection construction.
findings.minimal_repair: Replace the witness with: thicken an enumeration of Q into open dense U_n with mu(U_n) < 2^-n; the intersection is comeager and Lebesgue-null.

findings.quoted_text: forall future-inextendible causal geodesics gamma of (M,g) with finite affine length ; future-directed causal geodesics gamma: [0,T) -> M, inextendible in M, with T < infinity in affine parameter ; a future-inextendible causal geodesic gamma: [0,T) -> M with T < infinity in affine parameter ; future-directed, future-inextendible in M, with finite affine length
findings.why: The four fields do not quantify the same class of curves: 'future-directed' appears in D4 and singularity_definition and is absent from formal and definition; D4's 'inextendible in M' differs from 'future-inextendible in M'. A past-directed causal geodesic that is inextendible at its parameter end is included or excluded depending on which field is treated as normative. The affine-parameter convention itself is consistent (null finiteness is rescaling-invariant; unit speed fixes the timelike case).
findings.minimal_repair: Write one canonical definition (future-directed, future-inextendible in M, T < infinity in affine parameter, unit speed in the timelike case) and reference it from all four fields.

findings.quoted_text: either it admits no conformal completion of the declared kind, or some null geodesic generator of I+ is incomplete, or some ... geodesic ... is visible from I+
findings.why: D3 defines the completion family but asserts no uniqueness. The formal conclusion is exists-completion [(i) and (ii) and forall-gamma not-visible]; the informal negation treats one incomplete generator as a failure of the datum. That equivalence, and completion-independence of 'visible from I+', hold only if a completion of the declared kind is unique up to a boundary-preserving conformal diffeomorphism, which is never stated.
findings.minimal_repair: Add a uniqueness clause (or define P with 'for every completion of the declared kind').

findings.quoted_text: meager by construction; candidates that must be shown meager or explicitly excluded are: data with a nonzero Killing field, data in the exactly-extendible (Cauchy-horizon) family, ...
findings.why: 'meager by construction' asserts the meagerness result while excluded_set_status is unresolved and unresolved_items repeats that the meagerness is UNVERIFIED. The adjudication file cited by the schema (AMB-03) confirms the overclaim: the closed-proper-subspace argument 'is not stated by the schema and must not be assumed; excluded_set_status stays unresolved'.
findings.minimal_repair: Replace with 'candidates whose meagerness is not established here; each must be shown meager or explicitly excluded'.

findings.quoted_text: data outside the declared generic set are members of other classes (non-generic subfamilies) ; the schema does not decide membership of an individual datum ; two competent readers classify the same described spacetime differently under this schema ... the schema is imprecise and must be revised
findings.why: The three fields give different answers for one described spacetime in a listed excluded family (e.g. exactly stationary Kerr-type data): excluded_data says such data are members of another class, membership_ruling says individual membership is undecided, and schema_falsifiers[0] still declares any classification disagreement to be imprecision. The AMB-07 ruling added the membership rule without reconciling the other two fields.
findings.minimal_repair: Make excluded_data a set-level statement and narrow schema_falsifiers[0] to conclusion-level/class-level disagreement.

findings.quoted_text: G must contain data whose MGHD is future geodesically incomplete; otherwise the 'no visible singularity' clause has no content ; forall (s,delta) in D0 exists G_{s,delta} comeager forall D in G_{s,delta}: AF_{I+}(M_D) and complete(I+_D) and not exists visible_singularity_from_I_plus(M_D)
findings.why: The all-future-complete vacuity mode is now gated in non_vacuity (this repairs r1), but the gate is not part of the frozen formal statement: a consumer quoting statement_formal alone still has a statement satisfiable by a dispersing family, which is exactly falsifier.schema_falsifiers[1].
findings.minimal_repair: Add the incompleteness-witness conjunct to statement_formal, or declare that statement_formal is read conjoined with non_vacuity.condition.

findings.quoted_text: k is part of the assumption, never a conclusion ; gtilde = Omega^2 g of class C^k Lorentzian on Mtilde ; exists a conformal completion (Mtilde,gtilde,Omega) of (M,g) at I+
findings.why: The formal statement concludes the existence of a completion whose metric is C^k on the boundary, so C^k boundary existence is part of what is asserted for the data; only the value of k is fixed in advance. A reader can either claim the schema assumes the completion (it does not; forbidden_weakenings forbids assuming I+ complete) or that it concludes C^k boundary regularity (it does).
findings.minimal_repair: Reword: 'k is a fixed parameter of the class; the existence of a completion at that regularity is concluded, not assumed'.

findings.quoted_text: The class asserts hiddenness of singularities, not their absence.
findings.why: Presupposes that the class asserts the existence of singularities (hidden ones); the derivation comes from non_vacuity.condition. scope_statement is outside rule_spec.leakage_scan_blocks and outside the checker's ASSERTIVE_PATHS, so the R12 scan cannot see the strengthening (the tool now scans non_vacuity while the rule spec's list does not include it, a separate advisory inconsistency).
findings.minimal_repair: Phrase conditionally ('if a development in G is incomplete, that incompleteness is hidden') or move the claim into the scanned non-vacuity block with an explicit non-binding note.

findings.quoted_text: admissible regularity pairs: Sobolev variant s > 5/2 and delta in (1/2,1), or the smooth-with-decay default
findings.why: D0 mixes pairs with a non-pair default while quantifiers.ordered[0] binds '(s,delta)'; the smooth case carries no (s,delta), so the domain of the outer forall is not a set of pairs.
findings.minimal_repair: Bind a regularity-mode tag, or define D0 as the disjoint union of the Sobolev pair set and a smooth token.

findings.quoted_text: Swapping the first exists and the following forall yields the trivial statement that every data set lies in some comeager set.
findings.why: Rendering-dependent. Under the standard material-implication reading of 'forall (Sigma,h,K) in G' the swap is trivial (for each D choose G = X minus {D}; the implication is vacuous). Under a restricted-domain/conjunctive reading the swap yields the 'for all data' strengthening that genericity.class_change_warning calls a strictly stronger different class. order_matters: true is correct under both readings, so this is wording only.
findings.minimal_repair: State the reading in one line, e.g. 'with forall D in G read as forall D (D in G implies ...), no order swap preserves the statement'.

no_finding_categories: QUANTIFIERS: binder order, G-before-data binding, negation and negation_normal_form are correct; order_matters=true is not falsified. The load-bearing exists-G/forall-D swap changes meaning under every reading constructed (conjunctive reading gives the stronger 'forall data' class; material-implication reading gives a vacuous statement). The forall(s,delta)/exists-G_{s,delta} pair commutes only under a choice-function reading of the subscript (harmless, and not the pair the note is about). Only wording nits F14/F15.

GENERICITY STRENGTH ORDERING: rev4 correctly states that open dense implies comeager (open_dense_escape strictly_stronger; [open_dense_escape, residual_comeager] transfers), matching taxonomy line 141 and flash-15 genericity_matrix. This was inverted in the r1 revision and was corrected at 23:30:35.

AFFINE-PARAMETER CONVENTION: finite affine length is rescaling-invariant for null geodesics and unit speed fixes the timelike case; consistent across D4 and visibility.singularity_definition, apart from the qualifier mismatch F07.

COMEAGER vs FULL MEASURE, ABSTRACT CLAIM: incomparability is correct given a specified measure; the standard witnesses are a comeager null set and its meager full-measure complement. Only the recorded witnesses are defective (F03, F06).

VISIBILITY PREDICATE (degenerate readings): no degenerate reading of the predicate itself was found. q ranges over I+ only (blocks the spatial-infinity reading), I+ non-empty null with Omega = 0 and dOmega != 0 rules out an empty boundary, and J^-(q) is past-closed so whole-image containment is the standard 'seen from one boundary point' condition, strictly stronger than pointwise membership in J^-(I+). The defect is in the negation gloss (F02), not the predicate.

SCC ENTANGLEMENT: no derivation path from the conclusion block to C0/C2 inextendibility was found; forbidden_strengthenings, regularity.must_not_conflate and anti_scope keep SCC content separate. Black-hole formation is a different matter (F02).

boundary_cases_tested.case: A: Cauchy-horizon / C^2-extendible data with hidden incompleteness
boundary_cases_tested.description: One-ended AF vacuum data whose MGHD contains a Cauchy horizon, extends C^2 (indeed smoothly) across it, has complete I+, and whose incomplete causal geodesics are not visible from I+.
boundary_cases_tested.classification_under_schema: Ambient-space element; membership in G is explicitly not decided (genericity.membership_ruling) and is an open obligation (excluded_set_status unresolved; adjudication AMB-03). Conclusion-level verdict: not a counterexample; extendibility is explicitly irrelevant per regularity.must_not_conflate[1].
boundary_cases_tested.ambiguity_note: Against r1 this classification was ambiguous (excluded_set vs must_not_conflate). Against rev4 the membership_ruling resolves the membership question, but data_class.excluded_data ('members of other classes') was not reconciled and still supports a different reading (finding R1-F10).

boundary_cases_tested.description: Flat vacuum data (h = delta, K = 0, m_ADM = 0, development Minkowski, future geodesically complete, B empty).
boundary_cases_tested.classification_under_schema: In the ambient space; cannot serve as the non-vacuity witness (development is future complete); conclusion holds trivially; G-membership deliberately undecided. The schema's own adjudication_queue lists this as open row F1-AMB-01.
boundary_cases_tested.ambiguity_note: Declared-open obligation, not a hidden ambiguity; the residual textual conflict is the same excluded_data wording as case A.

boundary_cases_tested.description: One-ended AF vacuum data with a future geodesically complete development, B empty, complete I+.
boundary_cases_tested.classification_under_schema: Conforming instance whose censorship clause is trivially satisfied; not a non-vacuity witness; cannot refute the class.
boundary_cases_tested.ambiguity_note: Determinate; it exposes only that conclusion.statement_formal alone is satisfiable without the non-vacuity conjunct (finding R1-F11).

notes: The target file changed three times during this review (see revision_history_during_review); all findings were re-verified against the frozen rev4 sha256. Per the schema's own adjudication (hash drift ruling), the sha256 is the binding identifier, not the revision label.
The structural gate passes on rev4; every finding above is a semantic/content defect the gate explicitly does not decide.

The r3/r4 repairs fixed two of the defects in the revision described by the brief (open-dense strength ordering; B-based non-vacuity) but introduced finding R1-F01 by rewriting falsifier.tier_1 with an invalid single-datum refutation route.
